bluf: Fractl is a Delray Beach content and earned media agency founded in 2012 that sells organic traffic and AI visibility built from data journalism, digital PR and expert quote placement to Fortune 500 and high growth brands. Its headline case, Payless Power taken from no AI Overview presence to a top three cited brand within ten months, and five AI Overview and GEO case studies published September 2026 show where it is going: AI citation as the product. The Horus read is Favored (+33), best placed for KJ1, most exposed to KJ6. A rival should know its sitemap shows 1 URL updated in 365 days, it runs no ads of its own, the record names only 2 clients, and no rate card is shown.
doing:
The positioning line, a data driven content and earned media agency building the authority that grows organic traffic and AI visibility for Fortune 500 and high growth brands, decodes as: it makes studies and stories that journalists cite, and now sells the same citations as the reason AI answers mention a brand. The headline claim is a result rather than a credential: it took Payless Power from no AI Overview presence to a top three cited brand within ten months.

The sold mix runs 8 lines: organic growth strategy, strategic consulting and managed SEO, content development, data journalism campaigns, digital PR, expert quote placement, interactive tools and technical SEO. Two lead lines score 3: AI Search / GEO (the title and H1 target AI visibility; five AI Overview and GEO case studies published September 2026) and Content & Digital PR (the title leads with earned media; digital PR, data journalism and expert quote lines; 16 digital PR case studies). SEO scores 2 as a core line (strategic consulting and managed SEO plus technical SEO; SEO named in the homepage title). AI Automation / Agents scores 1 and every other capability 0: no paid media, no social, no data and measurement line, no web build. Breadth is 4. Proprietary items listed: an Agents tool suite, LLM Brand Mentions, LLM Citations, LLM Playground and Semantic Graph. The record lists no partners.

AI posture in plain terms: it frames AI visibility as earned authority, the same data journalism and PR it always sold, and publishes AI search studies plus a suite of free LLM agent tools; the Horus move read still marks P1 partial, because no audited product (tracking, scorecard, citation share) shows in the record despite the LLM Citations and LLM Brand Mentions tool names. The record lists no moves, no news and no jobs. Pricing signals: its AI visibility guide sketches how it would spend $20,000 over 90 days, with no rate card shown. Conspicuously absent for an agency built on publishing: a sitemap of 455 URLs with 1 URL updated in 90 and in 365 days, no owner or headcount, no ads of its own, and a roster of only 2 named clients against the 16 digital PR and five AI case studies its capability notes count.
clients:
Fractl serves a mixed book in fintech and lending, insurance, healthcare, SaaS and tech, travel, education, home services, energy and ecommerce, from Delray Beach, FL, listed as its executive HQ and only office; the positioning line names Fortune 500 and high growth brands as the target.

The record holds 2 clients, both with an observed need and none names only, which makes the book small but fully described. Payless Power came for AI and PR (a content marketing case on AI Overview presence for a prepaid energy brand, the same case the headline claim cites: from no AI Overview presence to a top three cited brand within ten months). Fanatics came for PR and content (a content marketing case study slug). The mix reads PR, reputation and content first (N12, share 0.545) and AI and automation second (N9, 0.455). The capability notes count 16 digital PR case studies and five AI Overview and GEO case studies published September 2026, so the case library is larger than the named roster; the record does not attach those other cases to client names, and a rival should treat the 2 names as the floor of the book, not its size.

Shared: Fanatics also sits on the book of vaynermedia.

What the base needs next: the Horus read ties it to KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers) as tailwinds and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) as headwinds. It is likely, moderate confidence, that clients buying citation presence next ask for a measured share of citations across assistants and a link from citations to revenue, which KJ9 says will be hard to prove and which P1 partial says the agency does not yet show as an audited product.
house: Say and do: 2 of 2 tested lines are practised on its own house. AI Search / GEO is corroborated: it publishes llms.txt and its sitemap holds 17 AI topic URLs. Publishing cadence is read as corroborated on 1 sitemap URL updated in 90 days and 1 in 365, against 455 URLs listed, a flat sitemap for a house whose product is published research; no AI crawlers are blocked. The Radar flagged no gaps. Tag stack gtm, meta_pixel, hubspot and rb2b; CMS WordPress; pixels meta_pixel; ABM stack rb2b; no test tools detected. Google Ads Transparency Center: none, 0 ads. LinkedIn: not found, 0 company ads and 0 thought leader ads (4 ads match the name query across all advertisers, none the agency's). It runs a Meta pixel and an rb2b tag while running no ads of its own, so its own demand capture reads as inbound. Meta and TikTok: no record. Social links list LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read gives a tailwind index of 33.4, band Favored, verdict Favored (+33). Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.681), driven by AI Search / GEO (+2) and Content & Digital PR (+1) against SEO (-1), and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers, net 0.292), driven by AI Search / GEO (+1). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net -0.225), driven by Content & Digital PR (-1) and SEO (-1) against AI Automation / Agents (+2), and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better, net -0.194), driven by SEO (-1). Best scenario fit: The Toll Road (72/100); resilience 31.9; integrity 100. Moves: partial on P1 (no audited AI visibility product), absent on P2, P6 and P7, unknown on P5; P3, P4 and P8 do not apply, since it runs no local, paid media or paid search line.

The Monsoon read gives index 60.4, band Onshore wind, inferred. Displacement 61.9 edges migration 58.9: the mixed book is slightly more price sensitive than the hours are movable, and SEO (20) and Content & Digital PR (19) carry the most movable hours. No hub office and no onshore claim is listed, so the footprint is inferred, with a shore split of 65% South and Southeast Asia and 25% Latin America.
openings: The computed openings are the unaudited AI visibility product, the unclaimed machine readable layer, the pricing silence and the KJ6 exposure. It is likely (moderate confidence) that the proof gap is the one to lead with: Fractl sells citation presence and names LLM Citations and LLM Brand Mentions tools, yet the read marks P1 partial because no audited citation share, scorecard or tracking shows in the record, so a rival with the audited number leads with it against a headline case built on a top three citation claim. The falsifier is a published citation share scorecard or tracking product appearing on frac.tl. It is very likely (high confidence) that the machine readable layer is open: P2 is absent, so feeds, schema and entity work sit unclaimed beside a lead AI search line, and a rival that pairs entity work with the earned authority pitch answers KJ1 on both sides. It is likely (moderate confidence) that a transparent, outcome priced offer undercuts it, since the only pricing signal is a $20,000 over 90 days sketch with no rate card, and displacement 61.9 says the book buys on price. Fanatics, also on vaynermedia, is the one contestable name; with only 2 clients on record, the question for the fintech, insurance and energy verticals it lists is whether the 16 digital PR cases have names behind them.
watch: I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures (late October 2026): growth below 10% flags cannibalization of its SEO line, and above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind its AI Overview cases ride.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility (late October 2026): US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend (rolling): the next $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM set the economics of ads inside assistants under KJ2, a line Fractl does not sell.

I1, Comscore monthly AI prompt share (Comscore Q3 report expected around December 2026): Gemini at or above 40% or ChatGPT at or below 45% favors S1, and no assistant above 50% with Claude and Perplexity rising favors S2, which decides how many assistants its citation work must cover under KJ3.

Follow up the five AI Overview and GEO case studies published September 2026 for named clients and citation share figures, which would move P1 from partial to making and add names to a 2 client roster.
